title: Managing group projects
examples: How do I make sure everyone contributes equally in a group?
What should I do if a group member misses a deadline?
What is the best way to handle disagreements in a team?

explain.say: Today we are looking at managing group projects effectively.

draw.text: Group Project Skills: Roles, Deadlines, Conflict

explain.say: First, understanding specific roles helps the project run smoothly.
For example, one person might take the role of the main researcher.
Next, setting clear deadlines prevents last-minute stress.

draw.text: Deadlines: Milestones keep you on track

explain.say: A real-life example is planning a presentation for class.
Conflict is normal, so learning to resolve it is key.

faq.q: What should I do if my group member refuses to do their part?
faq.a: First, have a private conversation to understand their difficulty. Then, suggest breaking their task into smaller, manageable steps.
asks: How do I address unequal workload?

faq.q: Is it okay to disagree with a group member's idea?
faq.a: It is fine to disagree, but always focus on the idea, not the person. Use 'I feel' statements to express your point of view.
asks: What if we have different opinions?

faq.q: How far in advance should we set deadlines?
faq.a: It is best to set internal deadlines that are one week before the actual due date. This builds in a buffer for unexpected issues.
asks: Should we give ourselves extra time?

faq.q: Do I need to take notes during group meetings?
faq.a: Yes, taking notes helps keep track of decisions made and action items assigned. You can also use notes to summarize disagreements.
asks: How do I keep track of decisions?

faq.q: What is the best way to assign roles?
faq.a: Consider everyone's strengths and interests when assigning roles. A quick discussion about preferred tasks can help achieve this.
asks: How do we figure out roles?

facts: Effective group work requires clear role definition for each member.
Setting interim deadlines helps manage the overall project timeline.
Conflict resolution focuses on solving the problem, not winning the argument.
Active listening is a crucial skill when handling group disagreements.

quiz.say: If you are the writer, what is your primary role function?

options.show: Designing the slides for the presentation.
options.say: Designing the slides for the presentation.

options.show: Checking all grammar and spelling errors.
options.say: Checking all grammar and spelling errors.

options.show: Gathering all the necessary research data.
options.say: Gathering all the necessary research data.

quiz.why: The writer is responsible for creating the actual text that forms the body of the report.

wrong.1: This is usually the role of the visual designer or presenter.
wrong.2: That task belongs to the editor.
wrong.3: Data collection is the researcher's job.

quiz.say: If the final submission is due on Friday, when should you set the internal deadline for the full draft?

options.show: The day before the final submission.
options.say: The day before the final submission.

options.show: The same day as the final submission.
options.say: The same day as the final submission.

options.show: Two weeks before the final submission.
options.say: Two weeks before the final submission.

options.show: The previous week, perhaps by the end of the day.
options.say: The previous week, perhaps by the end of the day.

quiz.why: Setting a deadline a week early allows time for review and revisions.

wrong.0: This leaves no time for unexpected problems.
wrong.1: This makes it impossible to review anything.
wrong.2: This might leave too much time and cause procrastination.

quiz.say: When a disagreement happens, what is the most constructive first step?

options.show: Asking open-ended questions to understand the other view.
options.say: Asking open-ended questions to understand the other view.

options.show: Immediately stating why your idea is better.
options.say: Immediately stating why your idea is better.

options.show: Changing the subject to something easier.
options.say: Changing the subject to something easier.

options.show: Waiting for the group leader to solve it.
options.say: Waiting for the group leader to solve it.

quiz.why: Asking questions shows you want to understand, which lowers tension.

wrong.1: This sounds confrontational and shuts down discussion.
wrong.2: This avoids the issue and means it will resurface later.
wrong.3: The group needs to work on solving it together.
